status_summary: Executive Order 14159 (signed 2025-01-20) directs DHS to authorize qualified state and local officers to perform immigration enforcement functions through 287(g) agreements or otherwise, to the maximum extent the law allows. Counts of agreements rose from roughly 135 in January 2025 (per an independent analyst and FWD.us, an immigration advocacy group) to 2,365 signed agreements as of 2026-08-21 and 2,510 as of 2026-09-15, according to news reports citing ICE's own tracker (as of 2026-09-15: 1,778 task force model, 553 warrant service officer, 179 jail enforcement model). FWD.us describes a September 2025 ICE offer to pay salary, benefits and other costs for trained task force officers, and a CRS report lists 287(g) coordination among the purposes of ICE funding in P.L. 119-98, with no separate dollar amount. The Mandate's two specific asks, a memo barring denial of access without good cause and a direction that ICE take custody of all listed criminal aliens identified by partners, were not located, so the match is partial; the growth in agreements is consistent with open access but does not show the memo itself.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion, signed; Section 11 directs DHS to use 287(g) agreements or other means to let qualified state and local officers perform immigration enforcement functions, to the extent the law allows.

Month-only date (first of month used): per FWD.us, ICE says it will cover the full salary and benefits of trained, certified task force model officers, plus startup costs, overtime and performance bonuses tied to immigration arrests.
An independent data analyst reports 1,202 active 287(g) agreements, of which 622 are task force model agreements, all signed in 2025, and roughly 1,100 signed since January 2025.
FWD.us counts 1,372 agreements across 1,169 agencies as of this date, including 764 task force model agreements, up from about 135 in January 2025.

CRS report on FY2026 DHS appropriations (updated this date) describes P.L. 119-98 as giving ICE about $31.1 billion, with expanding and coordinating 287(g) agreements among the listed purposes and no separate 287(g) amount.

Latin Times, citing ICE's own 287(g) tracker, reports 2,365 signed agreements in 39 states and two territories as of 2026-08-21: 1,640 task force model, 544 warrant service officer, 181 jail enforcement model.
UnoTV, citing ICE's 287(g) update of this date, reports 2,510 agreements: 1,778 task force model, 553 warrant service officer and 179 jail enforcement model.

title: Expand 287(g) partnerships with local police and bar denials of access without cause
uncertainties: ICE's own 287(g) pages could not be fetched (access blocked), so the 2,365 figure comes from a Latin Times report that cites ICE's tracker, and the earlier counts come from an advocacy group (FWD.us) and an independent analyst's data report; the counts use different methods (agreements versus agencies, active versus signed), so they should not be compared closely. I did not find or confirm a DHS or ICE memo on good-cause denial of access, or any custody policy for aliens identified by partners; the absence is not proof that neither exists. CRS describes P.L. 119-98 as the FY2026 reconciliation law; I did not check the statute text, and CRS ties 287(g) only to the ICE section's purpose list. The September 2025 funding offer is described by FWD.us, not by an ICE document I read. The match is partial because the program grew far beyond what the Mandate specified while its two particular asks were not found. Searches run: one search on 287(g) counts (an earlier search also covered the topic), plus fetches of the cited pages.
